\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਉੱਡਣਾ} (uḍḍṇā)}{ਉੱਡਣਾ (uḍḍṇā)}]{\pa{ਉੱਡਣਾ} (uḍḍṇā) — to fly}

\label{lesson:PA-C318-uddna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for to regret, then the Punjabi for to spend time.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਉੱਡਣਾ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਉੱਡਣਾ}} — \emph{uḍḍṇā} — \textquotedblleft{}to fly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\pa{ਤੇਜ਼} \pa{ਹਵਾ} \pa{ਵਿੱਚ} \pa{ਮੇਰੀ} \pa{ਟੋਪੀ} \pa{ਉੱਡੀ।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tez havā vich merī ṭopī uḍḍī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My cap blew away in the strong wind.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \pa{ਉਹ} \pa{ਪੰਛੀ} \pa{ਰੁੱਖ} \pa{ਤੋਂ} \pa{ਉੱਡਿਆ}, \emph{oh panchhī rukkh ton uḍḍiā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\pa{ਉੱਡਣਾ}} (\emph{uḍḍṇā}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{uḍḍīyate}, \textquotedblleft{}flies up\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Punjabi \emph{uḍḍṇā}, \textquotedblleft{}flies\textquotedblright{}, under it (CDIAL 1697).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uḍḍṇā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uḍḍṇā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tez havā vich merī ṭopī uḍḍī.} — My cap blew away in the strong wind.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Punjabi for to regret, then the Punjabi for to spend time, then say \emph{uḍḍṇā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \pa{ਉੱਡਣਾ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To fly\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਫੁੱਟਣਾ} (phuṭṭṇā)}{ਫੁੱਟਣਾ (phuṭṭṇā)}]{\pa{ਫੁੱਟਣਾ} (phuṭṭṇā) — to burst}

\label{lesson:PA-C318-phuttna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for to spend time, then the Punjabi for to fly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਫੁੱਟਣਾ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਫੁੱਟਣਾ}} — \emph{phuṭṭṇā} — \textquotedblleft{}to burst\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\pa{ਗਰਮੀ} \pa{ਵਿੱਚ} \pa{ਮੇਰੀ} \pa{ਬੋਤਲ} \pa{ਫੁੱਟੀ।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{garmī vich merī botal phuṭṭī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My bottle burst in the heat.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \pa{ਉਹ} \pa{ਘੜਾ} \pa{ਫੁੱਟਿਆ}, \emph{oh ghaṛā phuṭṭiā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\pa{ਫੁੱਟਣਾ}} (\emph{phuṭṭṇā}) is inherited from a reconstructed \emph{*sphuṭyati}, \textquotedblleft{}is burst open\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Punjabi \emph{phuṭṭṇā}, \textquotedblleft{}to burst\textquotedblright{}, under it (CDIAL 13845).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for saying what happened.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਟੱਕਰ} (ṭakkar)}{ਟੱਕਰ (ṭakkar)}]{\pa{ਟੱਕਰ} (ṭakkar) — a collision}

\label{lesson:PA-C318-takkar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for to fly, then the Punjabi for to burst.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਟੱਕਰ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਟੱਕਰ}} — \emph{ṭakkar} — \textquotedblleft{}a collision\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\pa{ਪੁਲ} \pa{ਉੱਤੇ} \pa{ਦੋ} \pa{ਗੱਡੀਆਂ} \pa{ਦੀ} \pa{ਟੱਕਰ} \pa{ਹੋਈ।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pul utte do gaḍḍīāṁ dī ṭakkar hoī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Two cars crashed into each other on the bridge.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\pa{ਟੱਕਰ}} (\emph{ṭakkar}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{ṭakkarā}, \textquotedblleft{}a blow on the head\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Punjabi \emph{ṭakkar}, \textquotedblleft{}pushing, knocking\textquotedblright{}, under it (CDIAL 5424).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭakkar}, once more

\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਡੁੱਬਣਾ} (ḍubbṇā)}{ਡੁੱਬਣਾ (ḍubbṇā)}]{\pa{ਡੁੱਬਣਾ} (ḍubbṇā) — to sink}

\label{lesson:PA-C318-dubbna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for to burst, then the Punjabi for a collision.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਡੁੱਬਣਾ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਡੁੱਬਣਾ}} — \emph{ḍubbṇā} — \textquotedblleft{}to sink\textquotedblright{}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਮਲਾਹ} (malāh)}{ਮਲਾਹ (malāh)}]{\pa{ਮਲਾਹ} (malāh) — a boatman}

\label{lesson:PA-C318-malah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for a collision, then the Punjabi for to sink.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਮਲਾਹ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਮਲਾਹ}} — \emph{malāh} — \textquotedblleft{}a boatman\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\pa{ਮਲਾਹ} \pa{ਕਿਨਾਰੇ} \pa{ਤੱਕ} \pa{ਤਰਿਆ।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{malāh kināre tak tariā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The boatman swam to the shore.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\pa{ਮਲਾਹ}} (\emph{malāh}) is a loan, usually traced through Persian to Arabic \emph{mallāḥ}, \textquotedblleft{}a sailor\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happened.
